episodes.about: Jensen Huang, the chief executive of Nvidia, has admitted to an affair with a top executive at the data center company Megaspeed - a woman going by the name of Alice Huang who the U.S. government alleges is a Chinese spy. In this special midweek episode, Kevin Roose and Casey Newton sit down with Stephen Witt, who wrote last year's Jensen Huang biography The Thinking Machine, to dig into what you need to know about the spiraling scandal and what it means for AI and the global economy.
episodes.title: The Jensen Huang Affair
episodes.why: Out today: Huang admitted the affair, and his biographer Stephen Witt helps sort the alleged spy, the chip-export stakes, and what the scandal does to the company at the center of the AI buildout.

episodes.about: Latent Space's first deep dive with an AI data company. In roughly a year, Handshake built an AI training business doing nearly $1 billion in gross annualized revenue. What are frontier labs buying? Garrett Lord joins with the people building that business to answer it in detail - what data the labs pay for, and why it has become a business this size.
episodes.title: What Frontier Labs Buy: A Data Deep Dive with Handshake AI — Garrett Lord & Team
episodes.why: The long one: Handshake turned selling training data to frontier labs into a nearly $1 billion-a-year business in about a year; this is the detailed account of what labs actually buy.

episodes.about: Neuroscientist David Eagleman sits down for a face-to-face conversation about why artificial neural networks simplified the cellular complexity of human neurons, and why AI's success forced him to reconsider whether intelligence requires the brain's biological complexity. They cover the brain as a neural parliament of competing drives, why he connects AI hallucinations to creative hypothesis-making, his case for AI-driven governance - including an AI president and citizen-specific agents representing voters - why dreams may defend the brain's visual territory, and how AI could accelerate answers to neuroscience's open questions.
episodes.show: AI and the Future of Work
episodes.title: David Eagleman, Neuroscientist and Author, on the Brain as a Neural Parliament, AI Hallucinations, and Rethinking Democracy with AI
episodes.why: Discovery pick — AI and the Future of Work is a long-running interview show about AI in the workplace, new here: Eagleman on the brain as a team of rivals, hallucinations as hypotheses, and whether an AI should govern.

episodes.about: AI agents are being pitched for almost every part of sales, marketing, and customer support, from AI SDRs to support bots that resolve tickets without a person - but most businesses want more leads, closed deals, and happier customers, not agents for their own sake. HubSpot CPTO Duncan Lennox explains where agents are actually working: support agents resolving over 70% of tickets, how to build enough trust to let an agent talk to your customers, context engineering and evals, a humanity score for avoiding AI slop, model-agnostic agent harnesses, and controlling AI costs.
episodes.title: # 386 Sales and Marketing Don't Care About Agents | Duncan Lennox, CPTO at HubSpot
episodes.why: Discovery pick — DataFramed is DataCamp's data and AI interview show, new here: HubSpot's product and technology chief on agents that already resolve over 70% of support tickets, and the humanity score meant to keep them from sounding like slop.

episodes.about: Would you hand a stranger your bank passwords, your private messages, and control of your personal information? That is the ask when the stranger is an AI agent, like Meta Muse, Claude Duet, or OpenAI Dots. In this Open to Debate episode, recorded live at the Masters of Scale Summit, Signal president Meredith Whittaker argues the convenience comes at the cost of privacy, since agents need sweeping access that could undermine encryption, expose personal data, and create new vulnerabilities for hackers. Neil Chilson, head of AI policy at the Abundance Institute, counters that existing laws, competition, and targeted safeguards can manage the risks without giving up the productivity gains.
episodes.title: Open to Debate: should we trust AI agents with our information?
episodes.why: Signal's president debates an AI-policy advocate over agents like Muse, Duet, and Dots: whether the sweeping access they need can sit safely next to encryption and private messages.
